title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges
body_markdown:
AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges to help improve the security posture of your VPN tunnels. This feature supports your migration to post-quantum cryptography based on NIST guidelines.


AWS Site-to-Site VPN is a fully managed service that creates an encrypted connection between your data center or branch office and your AWS resources using IPsec tunnels. With AWS Site-to-Site VPN, you can now configure post-quantum key exchange methods in your VPN tunnel options using the CreateVpnConnection and ModifyVpnTunnelOptions APIs.


There is no additional charge for using post-quantum key exchanges. This capability is available in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where AWS Site-to-Site VPN is available. To learn more, visit the[AWS Site-to-Site VPN documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/data-protection.html) .
